input.quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: Section 20 meets the preferred position in full. Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer and its Affiliates for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims (20.1) and for Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud (20.2). Standard procedure is mutual and workable (20.4: prompt notice, cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense, control of defence, prejudice-based delay standard, settlement consent). Customer's indemnity (20.3) is appropriately narrow — unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorised, and Customer's violation of Applicable Law — with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications and instructions. Infringement remedies (procure/modify/replace/refund) in 20.5 are in Customer's favour and Vendor may not terminate unaffected Services. Vendor's indemnity is not subject to a super-cap: indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims under 21.3 and therefore uncapped, which is better than the fallback. Note only that 20.1 contains no Customer-modification/combination exclusions, which is more favourable to us than the fallback contemplates.
